item: One extraction at a time, process-wide: a lock around the whole extract_article call tree, because libxml2 aborted the collector in lxml's document_fromstring under about 50 workers and the cause is not established
key_paths: src/ingest/extract.py; tests/test_extract_lock.py; scripts/analysis/collect_throughput_bench.py; docs/ledger/OPEN_QUEUE.md; pyproject.toml; configs/external_artifacts.yml; tests/test_external_freshness.py; docs/maintenance/EXTERNAL_DEPENDENCIES.md; src/ingest/lock_stats.py; src/monitoring/collect_perf.py; src/scheduler/runner.py; tests/test_extract_lock_stats.py; tests/test_sink_sweep_records.py
summary: The 2026-10-14 SIGABRT (lxml/html/__init__.py:740 <- trafilatura load_html <- bare_extraction <- extract_article, ~50 workers, 1 boot in 7) has no known upstream cause; the evidence is inferred from line numbers (trafilatura 2.3.1, lxml 6.1.3), the one loose match (trafilatura #840) is a release older than that. A process-wide RLock now covers the whole call tree so concurrent use of libxml2 is impossible from the app and every tree is freed inside the lock, on a return and on a raise. Measured on 4 CPUs: unlocked threaded extraction is 3.8-4.5x (2.2.0) / 2.7-3.3x (2.3.1) SLOWER than locked from 4 threads up (cause isolated 2026-10-17: the GIL hand-off of very many short GIL-releasing calls, CPU not waiting, reproduced without lxml), the whole pass is no worse locked within ~10% noise (0.51/2.45/3.92 vs 0.51/2.40/3.77 articles/s at 1/8/50 workers, 1.5 s fetch delay). tests/test_extract_lock.py (55 tests, 9/9 module mutants killed) pins serialisation of both paths, release on a raise, re-entrancy, trees freed under the lock and an AST walk that nothing else in src/ reaches libxml2. Built with it (coordinator's ruling): trafilatura>=2.1.0 in pyproject, registry entry trafilatura-floor and a test tying pyproject, registry and requirements.lock in one commit; it changes nothing for the machine that aborted (it ran a newer release), and the floor was run by hand only. Also measured on trafilatura 2.3.1: unlocked 262.5/96.8/101.1/98.4 vs locked 276.3/320.4/291.1/267.2 articles/s at 1/4/16/50 threads. THE TAIL: one long page holds the lock for every extraction with no timeout (nav-heavy 1 MB 6.2 s, 5 MB 34.7 s, 10 MB 85.3 s; the fetcher admits 10 MiB), shipped with that limit documented. Each monitored collect pass now carries extraction_lock (holds, longest and total wait and hold, page size behind the longest hold; numbers only) in its collect_perf.jsonl summary line and in its run report (scheduler.recent_runs, 30 runs, slim bundle included; the slim perf ring keeps only 20 lines), so an 85 s hold reads as a long page, not a stalled collector; tests/test_extract_lock_stats.py: 25 tests, 28 of 29 mutants killed (one equivalent). NOT built: subprocess isolation (OPEN_QUEUE: only if an abort recurs under the lock).
